vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: social-media-autopilot-api
Version: 1.1.1

The skill bundle provides a legitimate set of CLI tools for interacting with the SocialEcho social media management API. The code in 'client.js' and various command scripts (e.g., 'account.js', 'publish-article.js') follows standard Node.js patterns for HTTP requests and argument parsing, requiring explicit API keys via command-line arguments. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized file access, or malicious prompt injection was found; the functionality aligns perfectly with the stated purpose of managing social media accounts and posts.

llm.summary: The package appears to be a coherent CLI client for the SocialEcho API, but the registry metadata omits the required Team API key and the source/owner is unknown — there is a risk (and mismatch) you should understand before installing or running it with secrets.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, OpenAPI, and code files align: this is a CLI helper for SocialEcho's social media API (team, accounts, articles, reports, upload URL, Reddit communities, Pinterest boards, and publishing). The code only calls the declared API host by default (https://api.socialecho.net). However the registry declares no required credential while the code and SKILL.md clearly require a Team API key (--api-key). This metadata omission is an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts instruct the agent/user to call remote APIs via CLI args (no auto-reading of env vars). The runtime instructions and code limit actions to: read an optional local payload JSON, read bundled docs, and make HTTP(S) calls to the API. There is one caveat: the CLI accepts --base-url to override the API endpoint; if set to an attacker-controlled URL it would cause the supplied API key and payloads to be sent elsewhere. The code also expects GET requests with JSON body (explained in docs) and will exit non-zero when required args are missing.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only in registry) and package files are simple Node scripts relying only on Node builtins. package.json has no external dependencies. No remote downloads or post-install scripts were found, so install-time risk is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a Team API key at runtime (SKILL.md instructs creating a team API key and all request code requires --api-key), but the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential; this mismatch is a red flag. Additionally, the CLI allows --base-url overrides which would let an adversary capture any provided API key or payload if the user points it to a malicious endpoint. The skill does not try to read other env vars or filesystem locations beyond an explicitly provided payload file and bundled docs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and there is no behavior that modifies other skills or system-wide settings. The scripts only read local files (payload and bundled markdown) and make outbound requests; they do not persist credentials or alter agent config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is a straightforward CLI client for SocialEcho, but there are two practical concerns you should weigh before using it with real credentials: 1) Registry metadata does not declare the Team API key even though the code and SKILL.md require --api-key; treat that as a metadata/packaging error and verify the expected auth flow before providing secrets. 2) The CLI permits overriding --base-url — do not point it to unknown endpoints (an attacker-controlled base URL would receive your API key and payload). Because the source/homepage is missing, prefer running this in an isolated environment (or inspect and run the scripts locally) and use a scoped, revocable team API key with minimal privileges. If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for a verified source/homepage, or request that the registry metadata be updated to declare the required credential (primaryEnv) and a trusted homepage.
